name: Journal of Accountancy (AICPA) on AI in Accounting: Audit, Risk and Assurance
title: Journal of Accountancy (AICPA) on AI in Accounting: Audit, Risk and Assurance
answer: The Journal of Accountancy, published by the AICPA, is running sustained coverage of how artificial intelligence is changing accounting practice. Its most useful thread is the profession's move toward assurance over AI itself, with AICPA staff describing CPAs as well placed to evaluate AI systems, alongside practical guidance on hallucinations, deepfake fraud and agentic AI in audit and advisory work.

sections.body: The Journal of Accountancy is the AICPA's publication, and the pages read here are its own articles, news items, a report and a podcast page, dated from May 2024 through April 2026. They cover AI risk guidance for CPAs, client disclosure questions, agentic AI, AI-enabled fraud, how finance teams use AI, AI in audit, and the emerging role of CPAs as evaluators of AI systems. The material is written for a professional accounting audience rather than for technology specialists.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The coverage treats AI as both a working tool and a new source of risk. Guidance articles walk through hallucinations, where generative AI fabricates an answer such as a law that does not exist, and recommend asking the tool to cite sources and then having a human check them. They also flag sycophantic responses, black box opacity, and deepfake fraud, including a case where scammers deepfaked a CFO and asked a controller to make a large transfer. On disclosure, the Journal notes that no federal law or professional standard specifically requires CPAs to tell clients they used generative AI, while the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, some state laws including California and Utah, the EU AI Act and AICPA tax standards may bear on client data. Agentic AI is described as autonomous, goal-setting and adaptive, with predictions that within one to three years it will automate parts of client advisory services, bookkeeping, report generation and real-time auditing with better anomaly detection. Audit coverage describes generative AI drafting memos, processing documents and building visualizations, Caseware's AiDA assistant, and the Dynamic Audit Solution built with the AICPA and CPA.com. A report on CPAs as AI system evaluators quotes AICPA staff saying the profession is well positioned for assurance engagements over AI.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The Journal cites a Gartner report finding close to 60% of finance teams piloting or fully implementing AI projects but only 7% of CFOs reporting a strong impact. It reports cybercrime projected to cost more than $10 trillion worldwide by 2025, an alleged $35 million voice-mimic theft in 2020, and a $243,000 deepfake CEO transfer in the UK. Pinaka AI is said to predict late B2B invoice payment with 96% accuracy, and CREW Network is described as having 35 employees, some 50 entity charts of accounts and over 10,000 general ledger lines a month. The ABA's July 29, 2024 opinion on generative AI tools is cited on a lawyer's duty of competent representation.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in accounting gets the profession's own framing of where the technology is landing: in audit workpapers, advisory services, bookkeeping and fraud detection, and in a new assurance market where CPAs evaluate AI systems for bias, governance and functionality. The disclosure article is directly useful for firms deciding what to tell clients, and the risk guidance gives concrete mitigations for hallucinations and deepfakes. The AICPA's involvement in the Dynamic Audit Solution and its staff comments on assurance over AI show the institute shaping standards and platforms, not just commenting on them.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Accounting

sections.body: This is trade journalism and institute communication rather than research or a standard. Several items are predictions attributed to named consultants, and the finance team examples rest on a small number of leaders and vendors. The disclosure article states that no specific federal law or professional standard mandates disclosure, so its guidance is advisory. Some pages are podcast or column pages that point to related articles rather than carrying full analysis, and the material spans 2024 to 2026, so figures and product descriptions may date.
